```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 4.5, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)
source("case-helpers.R")
fmt <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
```

# Estimation backends on Email-EU-core

`rem()` fits the same case-control data with three backends: conditional
logistic regression (`method = "clogit"`), a neural conditional-logistic model
(`method = "nn"`) with either a multilayer perceptron or an additive B-spline
predictor, and a penalised degenerate-logistic model (`method = "gam"`) that
admits time-varying effects. This article fits all of them to the
`email_eu_core` log, compares their predictions on held-out events, and shows
the effect curves each backend estimates.

## Data and case-control sample

To keep the page quick to build, the analysis uses the first 3,000 emails of
the log. Each email is matched with three sampled non-events, and five
endogenous statistics are computed for every row from the history of observed
emails before it. The three counts are put on a `log1p()` scale; the time since
the last email on the same dyad is mapped to a recency weight with
`transform_recency()`, with weight 0 for a dyad that has not fired yet.

```{r data}
data(email_eu_core)
eu <- email_eu_core[seq_len(3000), ]
c(emails = nrow(eu), days = round(max(eu$time)),
  actors = length(unique(c(eu$sender, eu$receiver))))

stats <- c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count", "sender_outdegree",
           "receiver_indegree", "recency")
cc   <- sample_non_events(eu, n_controls = 3, seed = 1)
feat <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = stats)
feat$recency <- transform_recency(feat$recency)
feat$recency[is.na(feat$recency)] <- 0
for (s in setdiff(stats, "recency")) feat[[s]] <- log1p(feat[[s]])
```

```{r network-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.6, fig.alt = "Email network of the first 3,000 emails among the actors of the busiest pairs, each actor's three strongest ties"}
pairs_n <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(eu))), list(from = eu$sender, to = eu$receiver), sum)
pairs_n <- pairs_n[pairs_n$from != pairs_n$to, ]
und <- transform(pairs_n, a = pmin(from, to), b = pmax(from, to))
und <- aggregate(list(w = und$w), und[c("a", "b")], sum)
und <- und[order(-und$w), ]
ids <- head(unique(as.vector(rbind(und$a, und$b))), 60)
keep <- unique(unlist(lapply(ids, function(i) {
  r <- which((und$a == i | und$b == i) & und$a %in% ids & und$b %in% ids); head(r[order(-und$w[r])], 3) })))
bb <- und[keep, ]
lay <- withr::with_preserve_seed(layout_graph(data.frame(from = bb$a, to = bb$b, w = bb$w), ids = ids))
gc <- group_colours(lay$group)
act <- table(c(eu$sender, eu$receiver))
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),
                    col = gc[as.character(lay$group)], label = NA)
ed <- pairs_n[paste(pairs_n$from, pairs_n$to) %in% c(paste(bb$a, bb$b), paste(bb$b, bb$a)), ]
same <- lay$group[match(ed$from, lay$id)] == lay$group[match(ed$to, lay$id)]
ed$col <- ifelse(same, gc[as.character(lay$group[match(ed$from, lay$id)])], "#B4BBC0")
par(mar = c(1.8, 0.4, 2.8, 0.4))
draw_network(nodes, ed, directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 3)
title_left(sprintf("Who emails whom in the first %s emails", fmt(nrow(eu), 0)),
           "the 60 actors of the busiest pairs, each actor's three strongest ties; arrow: direction, width: emails")
mtext("dot size: emails sent and received  \u00b7  colour: group (modularity); grey lines join different groups",
      side = 1, line = 0.6, cex = 0.62, col = ink_soft)
```

The strata are split in time: the first 80% of the emails train the models,
the last 20% are held out.

```{r split}
cut   <- stats::quantile(unique(feat$stratum), 0.8)
train <- feat[feat$stratum <= cut, ]
test  <- feat[feat$stratum >  cut, ]
c(train_events = length(unique(train$stratum)),
  test_events  = length(unique(test$stratum)))

fm <- event ~ reciprocity_count + transitivity_count + sender_outdegree +
  receiver_indegree + recency
```

## Conditional logistic regression

```{r clogit}
fit_cl <- rem(fm, data = train, method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")
round(summary(fit_cl)$coefficients[, c("coef", "se(coef)", "z")], 3)
```

## Neural backends

`method = "nn"` trains on the same partial likelihood. A fraction of the
training strata (`validation = 0.2`) is held back for early stopping.
`nn_control()` selects the architecture: a multilayer perceptron scores the
five statistics jointly, while `architecture = "additive_spline"` fits one
B-spline curve per statistic and adds them.

```{r nn}
fit_mlp <- rem(fm, data = train, method = "nn", stratum = "stratum",
               nn = nn_control(hidden = c(16, 8), epochs = 150,
                               patience = 10, seed = 1))
fit_add <- rem(fm, data = train, method = "nn", stratum = "stratum",
               nn = nn_control(architecture = "additive_spline", spline_df = 8,
                               epochs = 300, seed = 1))
fit_mlp$fit
fit_add$fit
```

The perceptron stopped at epoch `r fit_mlp$fit$best_epoch`; the spline model's
best validation loss was at epoch `r fit_add$fit$best_epoch` of the
`r fit_add$fit$control$epochs` allowed`r if (fit_add$fit$best_epoch == fit_add$fit$control$epochs) ", so its training stopped at the epoch limit rather than by early stopping" else ""`.

## Held-out comparison

On the held-out emails each model scores the event and its three controls. The
table reports the share of strata in which the event gets the highest score
(ties split evenly), and the mean log partial likelihood per held-out event.
A model that ignores the covariates ranks the event first in one stratum out of
four.

```{r compare}
score_clogit <- function(d) as.vector(as.matrix(d[, stats]) %*% coef(fit_cl))
scores <- list(clogit          = score_clogit(test),
               nn_mlp          = predict(fit_mlp$fit, test),
               nn_spline       = predict(fit_add$fit, test))

rank_first <- function(sc, d) mean(tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$stratum, function(ix) {
  s <- sc[ix]; e <- d$event[ix] == 1
  if (s[e] < max(s)) 0 else 1 / sum(s == max(s))
}))
log_pl <- function(sc, d) mean(tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$stratum, function(ix) {
  s <- sc[ix]; s[d$event[ix] == 1] - (max(s) + log(sum(exp(s - max(s)))))
}))
held_out <- data.frame(
  model          = names(scores),
  event_ranked_1 = vapply(scores, rank_first, 0, d = test),
  mean_log_pl    = vapply(scores, log_pl, 0, d = test))
knitr::kable(held_out, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r compare-numbers, include = FALSE}
best <- held_out$model[which.max(held_out$mean_log_pl)]
rng  <- range(held_out$event_ranked_1)
```

All three models rank the held-out event first in between
`r fmt(rng[1])` and `r fmt(rng[2])` of the strata, against 0.25 for a model
without covariates. The highest mean log partial likelihood on the held-out
emails is that of `r best`.

## Effect curves

Each panel varies one statistic over its 1st–99th percentile range with the
other four at their training means, and shows the change in score centred at
its mean over the range: the straight line of the conditional logit and the
partial-dependence curves of the two neural models.

```{r curves, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6.2, fig.alt = "Effect of each statistic under clogit and the two neural models"}
centre <- function(v) v - mean(v)
mu <- colMeans(train[, stats])
cols <- c(clogit = "#4A5560", nn_mlp = pal[5], nn_spline = pal[1])
nice <- c(reciprocity_count = "reciprocity count", transitivity_count = "transitivity count",
          sender_outdegree = "sender out-degree", receiver_indegree = "receiver in-degree",
          recency = "recency weight")
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(3.4, 3.6, 2.6, 0.8))
for (s in stats) {
  g  <- seq(stats::quantile(train[[s]], 0.01), stats::quantile(train[[s]], 0.99),
            length.out = 60)
  nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(mu, each = 60), 60, length(stats),
                             dimnames = list(NULL, stats)))
  nd[[s]] <- g
  y <- cbind(clogit    = centre(score_clogit(nd)),
             nn_mlp    = centre(predict(fit_mlp$fit, nd)),
             nn_spline = centre(predict(fit_add$fit, nd)))
  plot(range(g), range(y), type = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
  for (m in colnames(y)) lines(g, y[, m], col = cols[m], lwd = if (m == "clogit") 1.6 else 2.2,
                              lty = if (m == "clogit") 2 else 1)
  axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.7, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
  axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.7, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
  mtext(if (s == "recency") "weight" else "log(1 + count)", side = 1, line = 1.8, cex = 0.62, col = ink_soft)
  mtext("centred score", side = 2, line = 2.2, cex = 0.62, col = ink_soft)
  title_left(nice[[s]])
}
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = c("conditional logit (straight line)", "neural: multilayer perceptron",
                            "neural: additive splines"),
       col = cols, lwd = c(1.6, 2.2, 2.2), lty = c(2, 1, 1), bty = "n", cex = 0.85, text.col = ink)
par(op)
```

```{r curves-numbers, include = FALSE}
rises <- sapply(names(cols), function(m) sum(sapply(stats, function(s) {
  g <- stats::quantile(train[[s]], c(0.01, 0.99))
  nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(mu, each = 2), 2, length(stats),
                             dimnames = list(NULL, stats)))
  nd[[s]] <- g
  sc <- switch(m, clogit = score_clogit(nd), nn_mlp = predict(fit_mlp$fit, nd),
               nn_spline = predict(fit_add$fit, nd))
  sc[2] > sc[1]
})))
```

Between the 1st and the 99th percentile the score increases for
`r rises[["clogit"]]` of the `r length(stats)` statistics under the conditional
logit, `r rises[["nn_mlp"]]` under the perceptron and `r rises[["nn_spline"]]`
under the spline model. The spline curves change most over the lowest values,
where many rows share the value 0 (a dyad, sender or receiver with no earlier
email of that kind), and some have kinks there: the B-spline knots are placed at
quantiles of the feature, and with many tied values several knots fall close
together.

## Bootstrap bands for the neural model

The neural backend has no coefficient table. `nn_uncertainty()` resamples the
training strata with replacement, refits the network on each resample with the
same `nn_control()` settings, and returns pointwise bands for the centred
partial-dependence curves and an interval for the in-sample concordance. Fifteen
resamples keep the page quick to build; the bands are coarse at that number.

```{r uncertainty}
unc <- nn_uncertainty(fit_mlp, data = train, stratum = "stratum", B = 15,
                      seed = 1)
unc
```

```{r uncertainty-figure, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Bootstrap bands for the MLP partial-dependence curves"}
plot(unc)
```

`nn_uncertainty()` evaluates each curve from the 1st to the 99th percentile
of the feature, with the other features at their means.

## Time-varying effects with the gam backend

The `gam` backend fits a case-1-control design, so a new sample with one control
per email is drawn and widened to one row per email. `tv(x)` lets the effect of
`x` change smoothly over time; `tvnl(x)` lets it change in both time and the
value of `x` (a tensor-product smooth). Both are compared with the model that
holds the two effects constant.

```{r gam}
cc1  <- sample_non_events(eu, n_controls = 1, seed = 2)
f1   <- endogenous_features(cc1, stats = c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count"))
for (s in c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count")) f1[[s]] <- log1p(f1[[s]])
wide <- widen_case_control(f1, covariates = c("reciprocity_count",
                                              "transitivity_count", "time"))

fit_const <- rem(~ reciprocity_count + transitivity_count, data = wide,
                 method = "gam")
fit_tv    <- rem(~ tv(reciprocity_count, k = 6) +
                   tvnl(transitivity_count, k = c(5, 5)),
                 data = wide, method = "gam", time = "time")
aic <- c(constant = AIC(fit_const$fit), time_varying = AIC(fit_tv$fit))
round(aic, 1)
summary(fit_tv)$s.table
```

```{r gam-numbers, include = FALSE}
d_aic <- aic[["constant"]] - aic[["time_varying"]]
sm <- fit_tv$fit$smooth[[1]]
days <- range(wide$time_ev)
beta_t <- function(t) {
  X <- mgcv::PredictMat(sm, data.frame(.time = t, reciprocity_count = 1))
  as.vector(X %*% stats::coef(fit_tv$fit)[sm$first.para:sm$last.para])
}
b_ends <- beta_t(days)
```

The time-varying model's AIC is `r fmt(abs(d_aic), 1)`
`r if (d_aic > 0) "lower" else "higher"` than that of the constant-effect model.

```{r gam-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Time-varying reciprocity effect with a 95% band, and the time-by-transitivity surface"}
# the surface of a two-dimensional smooth as mgcv plots it (cells far from the data are NA)
surface_data <- function(gamfit, select) {
  grDevices::pdf(NULL); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off())
  pd <- plot(gamfit, select = select, scheme = 2)[[select]]
  list(x = pd$x, y = pd$y, z = matrix(pd$fit, length(pd$x), length(pd$y)))
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3.6, 4, 3, 1))
draw_smooth(smooth_data(fit_tv$fit, 1), col = pal[5], xlab = "day", ylab = "effect on the log-rate")
title_left("tv(reciprocity_count)", "coefficient of log(1 + reciprocity count) by day; shaded: 95% band")
sf <- surface_data(fit_tv$fit, 2)
lim <- max(abs(sf$z), na.rm = TRUE)
div <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#7A4E8C", "#C9B7D6", "#FFFFFF", "#A9D3D3", "#0E6F6F"))(64)
par(mar = c(3.6, 4, 3, 4.2))
image(sf$x, sf$y, sf$z, col = div, zlim = c(-lim, lim), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", useRaster = TRUE)
contour(sf$x, sf$y, sf$z, add = TRUE, col = alpha(ink, 0.7), lwd = 0.7, labcex = 0.7, vfont = c("sans serif", "bold"),
        method = "flattest")
axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("day", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
mtext("log(1 + transitivity count)", side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
title_left("tvnl(transitivity_count)", "contribution to the log-rate; teal raises it, purple lowers it")
yy <- seq(par("usr")[3], par("usr")[4], length.out = 65)
rect(par("usr")[2] + 0.02 * diff(par("usr")[1:2]), head(yy, -1), par("usr")[2] + 0.06 * diff(par("usr")[1:2]), tail(yy, -1),
     col = div, border = NA, xpd = TRUE)
text(par("usr")[2] + 0.08 * diff(par("usr")[1:2]), range(yy), sprintf("%+.1f", c(-lim, lim)), adj = 0, cex = 0.6,
     col = ink_soft, xpd = TRUE)
par(op)
```

In the left panel the coefficient of `reciprocity_count` is
`r fmt(b_ends[1], 2)` on day `r fmt(days[1], 0)` and `r fmt(b_ends[2], 2)` on day
`r fmt(days[2], 0)`; the band is a 95% interval. The right panel
shows the tensor-product surface of `tvnl(transitivity_count)` over day and
count; mgcv leaves blank the combinations of day and count with no data near
them, which includes the gap between a count of 0 and a count of 1 on the
`log1p()` scale.
